summary.title: Interaction experiment: when agents add interactions
findings: Final round on 10 new TidyTuesday datasets (big tech stocks, egg production, tornadoes, energy mix, Valentine's spending, Carbon Majors emissions, Rolling Stone 500, centenarians, Taylor Swift albums, Premier League), 38 tasks: 32 good, 4 ok, 2 bad. Direct, indirect and explicit update asks were all right; muted pointers were short and specific. The 2 bad runs added series tools (legend, hover focus, inspect-index) to 6- and 12-line charts nobody asked to interact with, 6 of 6 repeats; one sentence in principle 3 (the data needs it means moving closer; many series is not that reason) made them clean 3 of 3 while asked or described series tools and zoom stayed 3 of 3. Two library fixes from the renders: a reference rule above the data used to draw across the subtitle (the axis now reaches update reference values, and overlays are always clipped to the plot), and captions placed on a bar or slice now use a contrasting ink with no halo, like a value label.

Muted annotations (current skill, version 'muted'): 46 runs. Overview questions: all 13 kept the chart free of updates. Concrete questions: 18 of 22 pointed at the answer with one or two short labels, or were answered by shaping the data (a top-10 or 3-row chart, value-labelled bars). Labels were concise and specific ('Jun 13, 2022 · $5.006/gal', 'Cars 2 · 40%'), never bare tags or sentences. Room rule held when the chart type was fixed: heatmap cell outlined with no text (though off-screen on a scrolling 144-year grid, which validate_chart does not flag), Iceland labelled across the sea, pie slice labelled. Explicit and presentation update asks all still worked. Soft spots (ok): the agent swaps dense charts for simpler ones unless told the type, misses a pointer on a calendar and a cluster, adds endpoint labels to a shaded span, and still adds x navigate to some long series and inspect for a 'hover' request. 39 good, 7 ok, 0 bad.

Current skill (clean-updates): high-level principles plus what each preset is for, and updates only on request. Re-run on the 31 tasks that had issues or test recall, plus 8 update tasks: 30 good and 1 ok on the 31 (base: 13 good, 12 bad). Every no-ask task got no interactions and no updates. All 6 asked or presentation updates were made, both plain questions stayed clean, and set-viewport appeared only to open a requested interaction. The one ok is h-acc (inspect + zoom on a 9,132-point line when the user only asked to hover).

Setup: 80 chart requests over 20 TidyTuesday datasets, from experiments/annotation/input/datasets. 20 ask for no interaction, 20 name one, 20 describe a need without naming it, and 20 harder indirect requests. The harder set includes two tooltip traps (h-acc, h-bl) and three tasks a static chart can solve (h-cia, h-lead, h-peng). Model gpt-6.1-sol at medium effort, one run per task per arm, graded by hand by the session agent.

inspect-index overuse is real and the edited rule fixes it. The committed skill (base) added inspect-index in 15 of 80 runs. 9 were wrong: on a single series (acc-1, d-acc2, d-mar2, h-temp, h-cra), on a request the tooltip already covers (h-acc, h-bl), or unasked on two lines (h-uni, h-tra). Both edited arms add it only where asked: d-mea, gas-2, mar-2, bl-1, h-gas, h-mar. Every one of those 6 is a correct use, so the rule does not over-restrict.

Main remaining issue: questions are read as analysis sessions. With the inspect-index rule alone (edited), 5 of the 10 question-style no-ask tasks still got unrequested presets, for example 'Do more powerful cars cost more?' getting select + navigate. None of the 10 instruction-style no-ask tasks did. The cause is two sentences: the chart skill adds interaction_spec when 'the goal of the session is to explore or analyse the data', and the interaction skill's Step 1 treats 'a live view' as an invitation.

edited2 fixes that without losing recall. It adds two changes on top of edited. The interaction skill says a question is not a goal (the chart answers it) and that being shown in a live view asks for nothing. The chart skill says 'says they will explore the data with it' instead of 'goal is to explore or analyse'. Results: no-ask tasks went from 15 clean to 20 clean, all 20 direct and all 20 indirect requests still got the right preset, and all 20 harder tasks were graded good, including both tooltip traps and the three tasks solved statically.

Direct asks are solved in every arm: all 20 presets, including context-menu, long-press, brush-angle, brush-y and accessible-navigation, picked with correct options and trigger conflicts resolved (pan:false beside a brush). The only differences are on generic 'make it interactive' requests. Base adds inspect-index to a single line; edited and edited2 pick zoom and a brush.

Smaller patterns to consider: (1) redundant pairs, such as axis-highlight + click-group-focus on a heatmap (temp-2 in base and edited; gone in edited2); (2) navigate on axes 'xy' for time series where x alone fits; (3) navigate on a 13-point yearly series (d-mar2), where zoom adds little; (4) click-annotate added to a 9,132-point daily series (edited d-acc2).

Caveats: one run per cell, one model, and both skills loaded in the system prompt. Over MCP the interaction skill is loaded on demand, so real exposure may be lower. The 20 indirect tasks were too easy (every arm 19 to 20 good); the harder set is where the arms separate. All grading was done by one reviewer, the agent.
